content.text:
I submitted index 30 (Ni 0.17, Sb 0.83) as the best composition. Its EQE was 1.91%, far higher than the other two I measured, but only 3 of the 31 compositions got a merit measurement.

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 21 | 0.66 (NiSb2O6 composition) | 0.012 |
| 27 | 0.79 | 0.0007 |
| 30 | 0.83 | 1.91 |

- **The result is patchy.** Index 27, just below index 30 on the Sb axis, was almost dead, so the high EQE seems to be a narrow feature at the Sb-rich end rather than a smooth trend. I can't say whether index 28 or 29 would have beaten index 30.
- **The Ni-rich half (indices 0–20) was never measured.** I skipped it on the textbook view that nickel oxide usually conducts holes rather than electrons, which makes it a poor photoanode, but I didn't test that. The Gaussian-process tool actually pointed to index 0 next, because it knew nothing about that region.
- **The models didn't help choose.** MACE ranked NiSb2O6 as the stable mixed oxide, and XRD at indices 21 and 30 showed similar patterns, which doesn't explain the 160-fold EQE difference. MEGNet's band gaps (0.04 eV and 3.6 eV) were not usable for a 2.1 eV illumination energy.

I used 2 of the 5 XRD measurements.
